items.stem: How does SDM decide what a signed-in user is allowed to see and do?

options.text: The user's DA-* (Entra/AAD) groups decide it all — menus and data alike
Menus are shown based on the user's DA-* (Entra/AAD) groups; the data on those screens is then filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema — the full RACI-applied access
From a permissions table configured inside SDM itself
Everyone who signs in gets the same access

items.explanation: There are two layers. The menu options are made available based on the user's DA-* (Entra/AAD) groups, and the data that comes on the screens is then filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema — the full RACI-applied access.

misconceptions.a: Right for the menu, but incomplete: DA-* groups decide which menu options appear; the data on those screens is separately filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema (the full RACI-applied access).
misconceptions.c: Close, but the Permission tables live in DDH's 'Security' schema, not inside SDM. SDM reads DA-* group claims for the menu and relies on the DDH Security-schema permissions to filter screen data.
misconceptions.d: Different groups grant different menus, and the Security-schema permissions further filter the data, so access differs per user.

items.stem: A user gets a 403 Forbidden when opening a Staff screen. What's the most likely cause?

options.text: They're missing the DA-* AAD group that grants access to that area
The feature is broken and needs a code fix

items.explanation: In SDM a 403 almost always means the user lacks the required DA-* group — authorization is group-claim-driven.

misconceptions.b: A 403 is an authorization result, not a crash — the feature works for users who have the group.
misconceptions.c: A database outage would not present as a targeted 403 on one area.
misconceptions.d: Caching doesn't produce a 403; the group check does.

items.stem: Which statements about SDM's authorization are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Sign-in is via Entra ID using OpenID Connect (OIDC)
Menus are built from the DA-* group claims on the token, and the data on those screens is then filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema (the full RACI-applied access)
Two users can see different menus depending on their groups
DA-* group membership can never be changed from within SDM

items.explanation: SDM signs in via OIDC and builds the menu from the DA-* claims on the token, tailoring it per user; the data shown on those screens is then filtered by the Permission tables in DDH's 'Security' schema (the full RACI-applied access). The DA-* access is system-generated by Sync-DDH-AAD, but SDM CAN augment membership — the Standalone Group menu supplies it (e.g. Help-Desk temporary access) and the sync propagates it — so d is false.

misconceptions.d: You can influence DA-* membership in SDM via the Standalone Group menu: the edit persists to DDH, Sync-DDH-AAD generates/syncs it to the Azure DA-* groups, and it reaches the user at their next sign-in. SDM augments the system-generated access rather than managing it directly.

items.stem: Why might two CSSD staff open SDM and see different menu items?
rubric: The menu is built from the user's DA-* group claims (each link maps to a management task a group grants)
Different group membership → different management tasks → different menu
items.sampleAnswer: SDM builds each person's menu from their DA-* group claims — each menu item corresponds to a management task that some DA-* group grants. Because the two users belong to different groups, they're granted different tasks and therefore see different menus.
